extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and readers interested in journalism ethics, media criticism, and the 2004 U.S. election
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing standards and failures in television investigative reporting—especially the authentication and handling of documentary evidence in high-profile news segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: The report concluded CBS 'had failed to authenticate the documents properly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify documents before publishing: confirm typographic and technological consistency with the purported era, establish provenance, and use forensic document analysis. The page cites typographic anachronisms (curved apostrophes, superscripted abbreviations like 'th', proportionally-spaced fonts) as initial red flags and notes comparison with contemporaneous typewritten documents (example: side-by-side comparison with a Microsoft Word 2004 rendering).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forensic/typographic analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial doubts about the memos focused on typographic anachronisms such as curved apostrophes, superscripted abbreviations, and proportional spacing that were uncommon for typewriters at the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult qualified forensic analysts and typographic experts; examine font metrics, spacing, special characters, and mechanical imprint features; compare to known authentic samples from the same period and device types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source provenance and vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: The controversy involved Bill Burkett, who later admitted misleading CBS about how the documents came into his possession, highlighting failures to verify provenance and source credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thoroughly investigate and document how evidence was obtained, corroborate chain-of-custody, assess source motives and past behavior, and treat unverified, single-source materials with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent expert vetting and accurate representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The review found CBS 'had exaggerated the views of experts it had consulted on the documents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use truly independent experts, obtain clear, attributable statements, avoid overstating consensus or expert endorsement, and include caveats and dissenting expert opinion when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek out alternative perspectives and corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel concluded CBS 'had failed to seek out and interview others who might have offered different perspectives on the memos.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively look for and include sources who may contradict or contextualize the evidence; corroborate claims with multiple independent sources before airing explosive allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inappropriate intermediary roles and conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: The report criticized Mary Mapes for contacting a campaign adviser (Joe Lockhart) at the request of the source, which suggested problematic contact between reporter, source, and a political campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain independence from political actors; avoid acting as a conduit between sources and interested parties; disclose and manage any potential conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and enabling public scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS made the memos available on its website, which allowed rapid public and expert scrutiny that contributed to uncovering problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, release evidence or documentation to enable external examination, but only after sufficient verification; transparency can aid fact-checking but should not substitute for internal vetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt correction, accountability, and internal review
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS 'compounded the damage by stubbornly defending its reporting.' Afterward an independent review panel evaluated the affair and there were personnel consequences (firing/resignations, anchor stepping down).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When errors are identified, correct them promptly and transparently; commission independent reviews for serious failures; hold staff accountable and implement remedial process changes to prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight and newsroom verification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The affair exemplified failures of editorial oversight: inadequate authentication, ignoring expert reservations, and poor production decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and follow robust verification workflows for documentary evidence and high-stakes stories; escalate unresolved doubts; ensure producers and editors heed expert reservations rather than ignoring them.
